review_scope: Entire325-line seven-surface procedure and ten complete direct/nested reusables read. All183 candidates and non-candidate context reviewed; approvals/comment assessment, changed-head freshness, instruction branch, MCP evidence, setup/firewall independence, client and selection boundaries retained. No upstream commands or examples executed, adoption, rights, source-publication equivalence or native behavior certification.

claims.statement: The procedure declares Copilot cloud-feature scope; no client entitlement or actual role is verified.
Editorial redirects include older agent/review routes, but not the unmatched published route; route equivalence is not established by shared title.
Code review provides feedback and possible suggestions, and agentic capabilities use Actions; the concept reference remains separate source evidence.
Website code review may be available to unlicensed organization members only when an enterprise administrator or organization owner enables it.
The website procedure requests Copilot through an existing/new pull request's Reviewers control; review request is not review completion.
The source describes usual sub-thirty-second review followed by reading comments; typical latency is not a guaranteed deadline.
High/Medium/Low comment severity is prioritization metadata, not authoritative security certification.
Default Comment reviews are neither Approve nor Request changes and do not count as required approvals; configured approvals are a distinct behavior.
Suggestions can be accepted singly or grouped into a commit; accepting them is a code mutation requiring review, not automatic correctness.
Fix with Copilot requires both code review and cloud agent enablement, then a draft instruction choosing a new PR or a commit to the existing PR.
Humans may react, discuss, resolve or hide comments, but follow-up comments are not visible to Copilot and receive no Copilot response.
The REST request uses copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]; a bot-review request is not a completed or accepted review.
Reviews are manual by default; automatic reviews require separately configured repository behavior.
New pushes do not automatically trigger re-review unless automatic reviews and Review new pushes are configured; a prior review does not cover a changed head.
Manual re-review uses the reviewer's re-request control; no live re-review is requested here.
Re-review may repeat dismissed or downvoted comments; resolution is not durable suppression or issue remediation proof.
Lite effort is described as cost-efficient targeted review of glaring bugs, vulnerabilities and style, not exhaustive verification.
Balanced effort is described as deeper reasoning for complex/security-sensitive/cross-service changes, not guaranteed completeness.
Effort can be chosen per PR before requesting review or as a personal default; settings are not observed by source review.
Organization owners and repository administrators may set automatic-review defaults; the actor's actual authorization remains unverified.
Approval preview status comes from a fully read reusable rather than assuming general availability.
Overview approval assessments do not by themselves count toward merge requirements.
When approvals are enabled, an approving review can satisfy required-approval rules; this is distinct from an assessment or Comment review.
New commits dismiss an existing Copilot approval and permit re-request; current-head review evidence is required.
Approvals are off by default and configurable at enterprise, organization and repository levels; no inherited effective policy is inferred.
Repository administrators can scope which Copilot approvals count using file paths; not every approved path necessarily satisfies the rule.
Custom-instruction behavior is supplied by a separate fully read reusable and its nested head-branch dependency.
Relevant repository skills and MCP can be used in code review; skill directories live under .github/skills and review-focused names aid discovery.
GitHub and Playwright MCP servers are described as default enabled for this context; actual configuration, tool permissions and credentials are not verified.
Context selection/evidence and review-specific MCP enablement are separate fully read dependencies.
The reviewer uses an ephemeral development environment customizable by Actions setup; ephemeral does not prove sandbox isolation or absence of effects.
Review defaults to copilot-setup-steps.yml, but a present copilot-code-review.yml takes precedence and enables an independent environment configuration.
Review firewall rules exist at organization and repository levels, separately configured from cloud-agent firewall rules; one agent's rules do not prove another's network isolation.
Comment feedback is described as product-improvement input through thumbs reactions; this is not a training/retention or consent policy specification.
VS Code supports reviewing a highlighted selection through Generate Code/Review, displaying inline and Comments-panel feedback; selection review is not whole-repository review.
VS Code can review uncommitted changes through Source Control; resulting inline/Problems comments and usual latency are not a merge approval.
VS Code Apply and Go To Next applies a suggestion without automatically committing it; Discard and Go to Next declines it.
VS Code feedback controls and repository instruction dependency remain distinct from applying or committing changes.
The Visual Studio branch requires version17.14 or later; the other surfaces do not inherit this exact client requirement.
Visual Studio starts review from Git Changes, shows comment counts or no-comments state, allows edits/dismissal and removal of comments; no-comments is not verified absence of defects.
External Visual Studio enablement guidance is linked, not transitively reviewed.
Mobile requests review from a PR's Reviews section by adding Copilot; this request workflow does not define a local code-editing or approval guarantee.
Xcode requires Copilot Chat extension0.41.0 or later; the linked release is not downloaded or executed.
Xcode chooses staged versus unstaged changes, permits deselecting files and requires Continue; selected files delimit review coverage.
Xcode displays reviewed files and popup comments, supports navigation and Accept/Dismiss replacement code; these are actions, not correctness or full coverage proof.
JetBrains requires Copilot access, a compatible IDE, latest extension and sign-in; all are actual-target prerequisites, not inferred from file existence.
JetBrains starts review from the Commit tool window, presents comments, permits edits/Discard and comment navigation; comment dismissal does not fix the issue.
The CLI branch uses installed/authenticated GitHub CLI and Copilot access, not necessarily Copilot CLI desktop-session semantics.
GitHub CLI can request Copilot at PR creation by reviewer option or interactive reviewer selection; examples remain inert and no PR is created.
GitHub CLI can add Copilot to an existing PR, with an explicit PR number when not on its branch; branch context is not inferred and the command is not executed.
Copilot approvals are public preview and subject to change at the pinned source.
Repository-wide review guidance is in .github/copilot-instructions.md; instruction presence is not adherence or effective enforcement.
Root AGENTS.md provides repository context and intentional architectural/test conventions; upstream examples are not executor instructions for this review.
Path-specific instructions under .github/instructions/**/*.instructions.md apply to matching files; scope must be resolved before claiming coverage.
CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md and REVIEW.md are additional instruction sources when present; source precedence is not specified here.
Linked instruction guidance and nested head-branch caveat are dependencies, not silently replaced by file existence.
The example asks Spanish responses, a security-checklist reference and readability conventions; examples are not adopted controls and are not executed.
Review-focused skill names/descriptions, explicit MCP instructions and PR references make context use more likely, not guaranteed.
Per-comment attributions and linked-session MCP/tool logs are documented evidence for actual context use; configured servers alone do not demonstrate use.
Allow Copilot to use MCP tools when reviewing pull requests is enabled by default; disabling it preserves cloud-agent MCP while separating reviewer MCP access.
The reusable contains a dated editorial usage comment and SVG icon markup; markup is inert context, not a security control or reviewed-image permission.
The custom-instruction limitation reusable is an admonition wrapper around the head-branch reusable, not an independent policy strength.
The subscription prerequisite links account-access guidance; linked eligibility is not actual entitlement.
JetBrains requires the latest Copilot extension and links installation/marketplace guidance; no exact stable version is enumerated or installed.
JetBrains requires GitHub sign-in and links authentication instructions; actual authentication remains unverified.
PR review reads repository instructions, agent instructions and skills from the head branch rather than the base branch; malicious or changed head content must not be treated as trusted base policy.
